title: Numbers to 20: a ten and some ones
summary: Read and build the numbers 10 to 20 with two ten-frames. One more, the number between, and first, second, third.
guide: This studio is for Year 1. Your child answers by tapping counters and numbers, so no writing is needed. If they can't read yet, read the sentences to them.
The big idea: 11 to 19 are "one full ten and some more". 13 is one full frame and 3 counters. Children should see that the 1 in 13 means one ten, not one counter.
In the last mission children stand in a queue and we meet {{term:ordinal-number}}s (first, second, third…). "Seventh" means the seventh place in the queue; 6 people are in front.

engine.instruction-paint: Tap a counter to change its colour.

read-teen.title: What number is this?
read-teen.prompt: One frame is full. How many counters are there? Tap the number.
read-teen.hint: A full frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, …
read-teen.success: Well done! One ten and 3 make 13. 10 + 3 = 13
read-teen.model: The 1 means one ten: one full frame of 10 counters. The 3 means 3 more counters.

feedback.only-ones: 3 is only the second frame. Count the full frame too.
feedback.only-ten: 10 is only the full frame. Add the counters in the second frame.
feedback.one-and-three: A full frame is not one counter, it's 10. What do 10 and 3 make?
feedback.too-big: Too many. Start at 10 and count the second frame.
feedback.too-small: Too few. Start at 10 and count the second frame.
feedback.empty: Tap the number for your answer.

make-teen.title: Make 16
make-teen.prompt: Put 16 counters. Fill one frame first.
make-teen.hint: A full frame is 10. 16 is 10 and 6 more.
make-teen.success: Well done! One ten and 6 ones. That's 16.
make-teen.why: Ali made 16 with only 7 counters: 1 and 6. What went wrong?
make-teen.model: The 1 in 16 means one ten, so 10 counters, not one. 10 and 6 make 16.

feedback.too-few: Too few. A full frame is 10. Then put 6 more.
feedback.too-many: Too many. Tap a counter to take it away. 16 is 10 and 6.

one-more.title: One more
one-more.prompt: Here are 15 counters. Put one more. How many now?
one-more.success: Well done! One more than 15 is 16.
one-more.why: What is one less than 15? How do you know?
one-more.model: 14. One less means taking one away, so we say the number before: 14, 15.

feedback.too-many: Add just one counter. Tap the extra one to take it away.
feedback.too-few: You haven't added a counter yet. Tap an empty space.
feedback.one-less: 14 is one less. We want one more.
feedback.same: 15 was the start. We added one, so now there are more.
feedback.too-big: We only added one. Go one on from 15.
feedback.too-small: We added one, so the number must be bigger than 15.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

between.title: The number between
between.why: 18 is one more than which number? One less than which?
between.model: 18 is one more than 17 and one less than 19. That's why it's between them.

feedback.before: 16 comes before 17. We want the number after 17.
feedback.after: 20 comes after 19. We want the number before 19.
feedback.empty: Tap the number for your answer.

queue.title: Seventh in the queue
queue.prompt: The children are in a queue. The queue starts at number 1. Sara is seventh. Make Sara yellow. How many children are in front of Sara?
queue.hint: Each counter has its number under it. Make counter 7 yellow. Then count the counters before it.
queue.success: Well done! Sara is seventh and 6 children are in front of her.
queue.why: Why aren't there 7 children in front of the seventh child?
queue.model: Because Sara herself is in the seventh place. In front of her are only places 1 to 6: 6 children.

feedback.wrong-colors: Only one counter should be yellow: Sara, in place 7.
feedback.counted-her: You counted Sara too. Count only the children in front of her.
feedback.counted-behind: Those are behind Sara. Count the children in front of her, starting at 1.
feedback.too-big: Count only the children in front of Sara.
feedback.too-small: Count only the children in front of Sara.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.
